newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay sugar prices ease on low consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: Bombay sugar prices ease on low consumer demand.

text.p: Indian sugar prices lost recent gains on the local market on lower consumer demand and profit-taking, dealers said.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 10 rupees to 1,215/1,255 rupees while M-30 fell by 4/5 rupees to 1,255/1,336 rupees.
"Sugar was firm yesterday on expectation of a lower free sale quota for January but the rally eased out today in the absence of any fresh announcement," one broker said.
The free sale quota for December is 800,000 tonnes.
"I am expecting a quota of 700,000/725,000 tonnes," said Shantilal Dedhiya of the Bombay Sugar Merchant Association.
